body:
@sepo-agent /answer For now, sometimes there will be different sources of server side errors: 

1. 500 errors from pushing 
2. 400 (?) errors from auth key issuing 

I am collecting these issues 
- https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/26337370165/job/77533245853#step:10:1 
But it would be better if we could review the code and make it more robust

comments.body:
I reviewed the relevant paths. This is worth doing, but I’d treat it as a small robustness implementation rather than only adding blind retries.

Key findings:

- The linked run shows a pre-run thread-state push failure before ACPX starts, from `writeThreadState()` pushing `refs/agent-state/...`: [.agent/src/thread-state.ts#L310-L344](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/thread-state.ts#L310-L344). That path currently does a single `git push`.
- Main implementation and fix-pr persistence both flow through `commit.js` into `commitAndPush()` / `pushToRef()` / `pushBranch()`: [.github/workflows/agent-implement.yml#L257-L268](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-implement.yml#L257-L268), [.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L244-L266](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L244-L266), [.agent/src/git.ts#L91-L127](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/git.ts#L91-L127).
- The direct GitHub App token path delegates to `actions/create-github-app-token@v1`, so Sepo does not currently control retry/classification there: [.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/action.yml#L50-L57](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/action.yml#L50-L57).
- The hosted OIDC exchange has a `run_with_retries()` helper, but the broker POST uses `curl` without `--fail`, so HTTP 5xx/429 responses are not retried; they are handled only after the request completes: [.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/exchange-oidc.sh#L78-L97](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/actions/resolve-github-auth/exchange-oidc.sh#L78-L97).
- Other ref-state push paths have the same single-attempt pattern, e.g. scheduled state and memory sync state: [.agent/src/scheduled-activity.ts#L138-L143](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/scheduled-activity.ts#L138-L143), [.agent/src/memory-sync-state.ts#L194-L200](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/memory-sync-state.ts#L194-L200).

Recommended implementation plan:

1. Add a shared retry helper for child-process Git/GH calls, probably in `.agent/src/git.ts` and/or a small `.agent/src/retry.ts`.
   - Retry transient GitHub/server/network failures: HTTP 500/502/503/504, 429/rate-limit, connection reset/timeout, temporary DNS/TLS failures.
   - Do not retry deterministic failures by default: 401/403 permission failures, non-fast-forward / lease failures, validation errors, missing refs.
   - Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter, e.g. 3 attempts by default.

2. Route all Sepo-owned push operations through that helper:
   - `pushBranch()`
   - `pushToRef()`
   - `pushHeadUpdate()` indirectly through `pushToRef()`
   - `writeThreadState()`
   - `writeScheduledState()`
   - `writeMemorySyncState()`
   - install fork publish push in [.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L836-L843](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/install-fork-pr.ts#L836-L843)

3. Improve hosted OIDC broker retry behavior in `exchange-oidc.sh`.
   - Keep retrying GitHub OIDC token fetch on curl/network failure.
   - For the broker POST, retry 429 and 5xx responses.
   - Treat most 400s as terminal, but log the sanitized broker message. If the collected examples prove the “400” is actually a transient upstream classification bug, add a narrow retry predicate for that exact broker error string rather than retrying all 400s.

4. Decide how far to go for direct GitHub App token issuing.
   - Minimal: keep `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` and improve only hosted OIDC.
   - More robust: replace the direct app token `uses:` step with a local Node helper that signs the App JWT and requests the installation token with the same retry classifier. Since `.agent` currently has no Octokit dependency, this can use Node `crypto` + `fetch` without adding runtime dependencies.

5. Add focused tests.
   - Unit tests for retry classification and attempt count.
   - Git helper tests proving transient push failures retry and lease/permission failures do not.
   - Shell tests for OIDC exchange retrying 5xx/429 but not generic 400.
   - Keep docs small, likely update `.agent/docs/usage/internal-actions.md` to mention retry behavior for auth resolution.

I’d implement this in one PR, with the first pass focused on Sepo-owned push operations plus hosted OIDC retry handling. The direct `actions/create-github-app-token` replacement is the only part I’d consider optional, because it is a slightly larger auth change.

title: Adding retries for more robust service
